# Weave nesting fixtures

Fixtures for phase 06: structural selectors and nested rule lowering ([CSS-COMPATIBILITY.md §4](../../../docs/CSS-COMPATIBILITY.md#4-nesting-lowering-and-specificity)), interleaved declarations, group at-rules nested in rules, the at-rule context matrix for nested and recipe-produced at-rules (§2, §3), and preservation of unknown syntax inside rules. They are executed by [crates/weave-compiler/tests/fixtures.rs](../../../crates/weave-compiler/tests/fixtures.rs) (`cargo test`), and every case must pass.

The format and rules are those of the [CSS-subset fixtures](../css/README.md): exact bytes for successful builds (compiled twice, validated by the independent CSS parser), and exactly the listed diagnostics for error cases. The sources were written against the specification; the expected outputs were recorded from the compiler and then reviewed line by line against LANGUAGE.md §11–§12 and CSS-COMPATIBILITY.md §2–§4 (unlike earlier sets, they were not derived by hand before the first run). Their meaning does not rest on review alone:

- [crates/weave-compiler/tests/nesting.rs](../../../crates/weave-compiler/tests/nesting.rs) checks the specificity of every lowered selector, one and two levels deep, against the native definition (`&` as `:is(<parent list>)`) with an independent specificity calculator, plus cascade order, contexts and the expansion limits;
- [scripts/browser_check.py](../../../scripts/browser_check.py) compares computed styles of lowered CSS with native CSS Nesting in a real browser ([tests/browser](../../browser/README.md)).

Parse-time errors stop the build before evaluation, so parse-time (021) and evaluation-time (020, 022) cases are kept apart.

## Index

| Case | Expect | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| [001-parent-references](001-parent-references/) | css | Every `&` position of CSS-COMPATIBILITY.md §4.1: leading `&` with simple and complex parents, implicit descendant, leading combinators (also followed by `&`), `&` after other compounds, `&` inside `:not()`, `:is()`, `:where()`, `:has()` and `:nth-child(… of …)`, type and universal parents after other simple selectors, namespaced types, lists at every level (one output selector per nested selector, never a Cartesian product), and three levels of nesting. |
| [002-interleaved-declarations](002-interleaved-declarations/) | css | Declarations before, between and after nested rules and nested group at-rules become rule segments in source order; duplicate declarations stay; `opaque` blocks, unknown at-rules and `/*!` comments join the segment they appear in; segments without output and empty nested rules are dropped; `!important` and custom properties are unchanged. |
| [003-nested-group-at-rules](003-nested-group-at-rules/) | css | `@media`, `@supports`, `@container`, `@layer` and `@starting-style` nested in rules, in nested rules and in each other wrap the current selector; preludes are never merged; empty nested group rules are omitted while empty `@layer` blocks are kept; a nested rule inside an at-rule is lowered against the enclosing rule; a list parent stays a list in segments and becomes `:is()` only in nested selectors. |
| [004-recipes-and-contexts](004-recipes-and-contexts/) | css | Recipes and content blocks emit nested rules and group at-rules, lowered where they are expanded; `slot;` inside a nested group at-rule; `&` in a content block refers to the rule of the `apply`; `when`/`each` inside nested rules; at-rules allowed only at stylesheet level (`@font-face`, `@keyframes`, `@property`, `@page` with margin rules, `@layer` statements, `@scope`, `@font-feature-values`) emitted by a recipe applied at stylesheet level. |
| [005-stylesheet-at-rule-contexts](005-stylesheet-at-rule-contexts/) | css | Known at-rules at stylesheet level with nested rules inside their bodies: `@media` and `@supports` around rules with nesting, `@scope` bodies whose rules nest, `@layer` blocks, and unknown future at-rules preserved byte for byte at every depth (also inside nested rules and nested group at-rules). |
| [006-interpolated-selectors](006-interpolated-selectors/) | css | Interpolated nested selectors are parsed structurally after interpolation: identifier escaping, fragments containing combinators and lists, canonical spacing of inserted text, interpolated `&` positions. |
| [020-error-nested-selectors](020-error-nested-selectors/) | error | Nested selectors rejected while lowering: nesting under a pseudo-element (also a legacy one-colon pseudo-element and a functional one) is E6004; a type selector after `&` in a compound, an empty selector in a list, a dangling or doubled combinator and an interpolated type after `&` are E6007. Declarations and group at-rules under a pseudo-element are fine. |
| [021-error-nested-contexts](021-error-nested-contexts/) | error | At-rules that cannot be nested in a rule body are rejected while parsing: `@scope` is E6006; `@font-face`, `@keyframes`, `@property`, `@page`, `@layer` statements, `@import` and `@font-feature-values` are E6005. |
| [022-error-recipe-placement](022-error-recipe-placement/) | error | Placement of known at-rules from recipe bodies and content blocks is checked where they are expanded: stylesheet-only at-rules inside a rule are E6005 (`@scope` E6006); a group at-rule expanded in a declaration list is E6005; declarations from a group at-rule expanded at stylesheet level are E6001; a nested rule under a pseudo-element via a recipe is E6004. |
